questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good weather and loads of sunshine - and that it was far away, so it really felt like an adventure!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. UQ has a thougrough online guide that helps you!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Judy and Karen from the international team were helpful, but very slow at replying to e-mails. Furthermore the introdution week was really good and fun and offered all needed information!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Look at Scape or Student One. You can book 6 months in advance, and live in the middle of the city! Don't live in Toowong though. It is kind of far away from both campus and the city and a bit boring and lots of hills!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Student One is cheaper, but you get what you pay for. Simple rooms, but great shared facilities! Beware of the potential roomies though. A lot of Asians live in Brisbane - and cultural differences are big in terms of ways to share common living spaces.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Brisbane has loads of options of private student accommadation. It is expensive - but it is very easy to find somewhere to live.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to apply really early, which was kind of stressfull - but also nice, as you got all your documents early and could apply for visa early! There was a step by step guide by UQ, so it was easy to nagivate, but of course it took some time and effort.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help was available from University of Copenhagen, and UQ replied very slowly on e-mails, but there premade guides were good.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes, I got all the classes, I wanted!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. If you just do, what it says in the guide, you will be fine. And even if you do something wrong, they will not kick you out ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was very high and the courses weren't easy. Maybe a bit harder than on UCPH, because most exams were with no aids!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professors and tutors were way more engaged and interesting at UQ compareed to UCPH. The lectures and classes were really good - and all teachers cared deeply about every single student. You could even get private conversations with the teacher if you had a hard time understanding a subject!! It was a really pleasant experience!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Writing the Genre Novel, Introduction to Software Engeniering, Publishing and Professional Practice, Introduction to Music Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Publishing and Professional Practice was amazing!!! Generally all of their creative writing courses were so interesting and the lectures were so dedicated.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to buy duvets and pillows and all kinds of kitchen stuff for the apartment!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and buying coffee was very inexpensive - so I ended up doing it a lot and spend a lot of money anyways ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds! Sports, music, theater - everything!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate, because I was too busy with other friends and fun stuff.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: North Stradbrooke Island was very nice!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes - the australian culture is very similiar to UK/US culture and very easy to understand as a dane.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make friends in class!! And remember that all aussies love a new friend!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Figuring out how honest you could be - aussies are very polite!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed vibe in the city was amazing!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you want to spent your weekends having fun - choose courses, that give you the energy and time to do that. UQ courses are hard - so keep that in mind!
2) Bring some money down here. Stuff if not that expensive - but going out is a big part of the culture!
3) Know that Brisbane is a city with MANY Danish exchange students. We were around 30 in one big group chat - and it was amazing! but if you want to get far away from Danish culture, go somewhere else.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was amazing!!!! And the campus is so beautiful and calm with loads of nature!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making local friends!! And going to UQ. The campus is amazing and very green - and all classes were inspiring and amazing!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Realizing that you are not gonna be able to see all of Australia while you are here!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
